title: 1983 AHSME Problem 29
statement: A point \(P\) lies in the same plane as a given square of side \(1.\) Let the vertices of the square, taken counterclockwise, be \(A,\) \(B,\) \(C\) and \(D.\) Also, let the distances from \(P\) to \(A,\) \(B\) and \(C,\) respectively, be \(u,\) \(v\) and \(w.\) What is the greatest distance that \(P\) can be from \(D\) if \(u^2+v^2=w^2?\)

solutions.text:
Place \(D=(0,0),\) \(A=(1,0),\) \(B=(1,1),\) and \(C=(0,1),\) with \(P=(x,y).\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} &(x-1)^2+y^2\\ &\quad+(x-1)^2+(y-1)^2\\ &=x^2+(y-1)^2, \end{aligned} \] which simplifies to \((x-2)^2+y^2=2.\) Thus \(P\) lies on a circle centered \(2\) units from \(D\) with radius \(\sqrt2.\) Its greatest distance from \(D\) is \(2+\sqrt2.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Substitute \(P=(x,y)\) into the distance equation and complete the square
